title: Stepped cross-region failover playbook and customer escalation response
creator: Marina Alvarez
description: Playbook for detecting, executing, and validating a stepped cross-region failover with explicit guidance for Hosted and Dedicated customers, plus templated customer communications and post-incident follow-ups. Focus is on minimizing request loss, avoiding cascade failures from traffic shifts, and providing clear escalation paths for customer-facing teams.
runbook_steps: 1) Detect: automated alerts trigger when region latency P95 > 3x baseline or error rate > 2% sustained for 3 minutes.
2) Triage: SRE on-call validates alert against infra dashboards (edge gateways, LB metrics, model runtime errors, KV cache hit rates).
3) Contain: apply ingress rate-limits to suspected region and set short-term circuit-breaker for non-essential background flows.
4) Assess capacity: query capacity matrix for target region (GPU availability, queued slots, buffer headroom).
5) Warm standby: begin pre-warming model replicas and KV caches in target region with small synthetic traffic and recent prefetched prefixes.
6) Stepped traffic shift: increase traffic in weighted increments (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) with 2-minute observation windows between increments.
7) Validate: run smoke prompts and customer-specific test prompts through shifted traffic to verify inference correctness and latency SLOs.
8) Complete failover: when metrics stable for two consecutive windows, remove routing to affected region and update DNS with reduced TTLs where applicable.
9) Post-failover: rehydrate caches, monitor error budgets, and keep elevated telemetry retention for 72 hours.
10) Escalation: if any step fails, escalate to Incident Lead and trigger customer communication template.
traffic_shift_sequence: abort criteria: error rate increase > 0.5% absolute or P95 latency regression > 20% vs baseline
detection_triggers: oncall-manual: customer reporting increased errors from hosted/dedicated endpoints
mitigation_short_term: apply ingress rate-limiter to affected region (throttle non-critical routes)
enable model-variant fallback with smaller memory footprint in the affected region
route new requests to proximate healthy region using weighted DNS or traffic-router override
increase autoscaling headroom in target region (temporarily raise burst limit)
mitigation_long_term: harden traffic-steering logic with explicit per-customer routing safeguards
improve pre-warm pipeline for KV cache and prefix caching during any shift
add chaos tests for steady-state traffic shifts across hosted and dedicated fleets
instrument per-route warmup metrics and integrate into Console rollout guardrails
communication_templates: Status - Initial: Subject: Service degradation detected in region X; Body: We detected elevated errors/latency in region X. Our SRE team is executing a controlled failover to a healthy region to restore service. You may see brief retries or small latency changes. We'll update in 15 minutes with progress.

Status - Update: Subject: Failover progress: 30% traffic shifted to region Y; Body: We have shifted 30% of traffic to region Y and are monitoring for errors and latency. If you see issues, please contact support with your request IDs.

Post-incident: Subject: Incident resolved: Cross-region failover completed; Body: The controlled failover is complete. Root cause analysis is in progress. We will follow up with postmortem and action plan within 72 hours. If you require a private postmortem, please request it via your CSM.

postmortem_summary: Root cause: a regression in the traffic-router's per-tenant header handling caused stale session affinity to be misrouted during rapid weight changes. Combined with a recent KV cache eviction parameter change, this produced a spike in cache misses and authentication token churn for some Dedicated customers. We successfully executed a stepped failover to a warmed region, but gaps in the per-customer routing safeguards caused a dedicated customer to see auth failures until a targeted pin was applied.

ENG-15896: Revert/adjust KV eviction change and add slow-roll of eviction thresholds with telemetry
PM-428: Update runbook and Console controls to expose per-customer pinning during emergencies
DES-214: Create in-console guidance screens for on-call to reduce manual missteps during weighted shifts
SRE-ops: Build a synthetic customer test harness for Dedicated customers to exercise auth and cache behavior during shifts
test_plan: add e2e test: simulate 4 region weighted shift and validate per-tenant affinity preserved
create smoke scenarios for Dedicated customer that validate auth token persistence across region transitions
load test warmup path to ensure KV cache prefill latency under production traces
metrics_to_monitor: kv-cache miss rate and cold-start latency
rollback_plan: abort shift and return to last known-good weighting if abort criteria met
if persistent instability, re-enable traffic to original region at reduced rate while draining non-critical workloads
manual pinning for affected dedicated customers until root cause fix deployed
